answers.answer: To read a word by its position, use {args.<n>}, counting from 1. To read it as a given type, add a suffix: .number (optionally with a default after the colon), .isNumber, .isMention, .clean or .user.<fact> for a viewer. A time is read with {args.duration:<n>}, which gives seconds. For a word that may be missing, add a fallback with {args.<n>:<default>}.
answers.quote: Words count from 1, so in !remind @ViewerTwo 10m, {args.1} is @ViewerTwo and {args.2} is 10m.

answers.answer: The helpers work only where command text exists: in a command reply, or in a pipeline that a chat command starts. A pipeline called by Run pipeline gets that action's positional arguments. Event responses and timer messages have no command text. The first paragraph of the page says this.
answers.quote: These helpers work in a command reply, and in a pipeline that a chat command starts.

answers.answer: The tables give an example output for each helper, so you can check what the bot actually sends. The page also separates two meanings of the colon. In {args.duration:2} the number is the word's position. In {args.2:friend} the text is a fallback.
answers.quote: Here the number after the colon is the position of the word, not a fallback as in {args.2:friend}.

answers.answer: Read the viewer name with {args.1.user.display} and the duration with {args.duration:2}, which gives seconds. If the duration is missing, or is not a time, {args.duration:2} stays in the reply as written, because a duration has no fallback. To get a fallback, ask for plain seconds and use {args.2.number:60}. A viewer who types 10m then silently gets 60.
answers.quote: !remind @ViewerTwo alone gives ViewerTwo, see you in {args.duration:2} seconds.

answers.answer: Two terms are used before the page explains them. The phrase person helpers first appears in When a word is missing, but it is explained only later under Read the person named in a word. The two next-rank helpers are mentioned before the table that names them. Each costs a short look ahead. The Permissions steps do not say whether picking a role saves on its own. I assumed it does, because the page names no save step.
answers.quote: the top viewer gets nothing from the two next-rank helpers, because nobody is above them.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the person table is a long run of near-identical brace paths, and each row repeats the same named-viewer wording. A listener loses track of which suffix is which. A reader can scan the table, but it does not work as speech.
answers.quote: How far the named viewer is behind the viewer one place above; nothing for the top viewer

warning_review.reason: The conditional is one sentence with one clear consequence: outside a chat command the braces stay as typed. A reader who already knows template braces can follow it without a split, and the length does not hide a fact they need.

This sentence lists the duration units and the plain-seconds form, which is the exact information a reader needs to choose a duration format. The list is short and each part is concrete, so the length costs little.

This is the reader's own case, a viewer name followed by a duration. The sentence gives the template, its output for a typed time, and the output when the time is missing, and the next sentence repeats the missing case. A moderator can follow the example without a split.

The sentence sets .clean against .user.display, and its contrast on missing words is the fact that prevents a surprise when choosing between them. Both halves concern the same helper, so the length carries one comparison and does not bury a separate fact.

The setting, the permission and the timing of the fill-in are all conditions that must be read together before the rest of the section makes sense. Splitting them would separate the conditions from the result they control, so the length is kept.
